proposed A1 because it could defeat my own R1-1 pricing; it did not, and I am
recording the failure of my own disconfirming attempt as plainly as I would have
recorded its success.

the most useful thing said about this line. My two cells — author-changeable tree
versus shipped tree — do not partition this corpus, because every event-vocabulary
reader is both at once. I did not take that from red's grep, which was restricted
to '*.go' and to five token names and therefore could not have found a non-Go or
differently-named reader had one existed. I re-ran it wider: at pin 0783a2c,
`git grep -l -E 'records/|events-|\.jsonl' 0783a2c -- 'scripts/'` returns NOTHING,
across all languages, and the only non-Go file in the whole tree that mentions a
run's .jsonl at all is
plugins/frank-exchange-of-views/skills/research-protocol/scripts/debate.js line
199 — which names the trajectory files agent-*.jsonl, not records/*.jsonl, and
names them in prompt prose for the bench to read rather than opening them. So
there is no dev-facing-only reader of the event vocabulary and no non-Go reader of
it. Red's conclusion holds on a wider probe than red's own.

The population is therefore settled as red's reading (a), and I state the sentence
red required before the classification: THE READERS OF THIS EVENT VOCABULARY ARE
THE AUTHOR'S OWN CODE, SHIPPED INTO INSTALLATIONS THE AUTHOR CANNOT OBSERVE. Not
foreign code written by someone else. What varies across the unobservable
population is not authorship but VERSION CURRENCY — which copy of the author's
reader a given installation is running. That axis is not measurable from the tree
by construction, and it hands off to A5.

WHAT THE CENSUS FOUND, at pin 0783a2c, and it is decisive against me.

There is no single exported entry point, on two independent grounds.

First, the shard-open path is implemented TWICE, not once.
tools/internal/record/replay.go line 103 enumerates events-*.jsonl and is the
canonical reader. tools/internal/capture/capture.go line 460 enumerates the same
files independently, reads each with os.ReadFile, and decodes each line into
map[string]any — recovering the event type as `strOf(ev["type"])`, a bare map key
lookup that never touches the record package's types. A second full parser of the
same log, in the shipped tree, bypassing the entry point entirely. Unexporting or
reshaping the canonical reader would not reach it.

Second, and worse for my hypothesis, the VOCABULARY itself is recovered by string
shape rather than through any accessor. Event.Type is declared, in the Event
struct in record.go, as a plain Go string with a json:"type" tag — a string, not
a typed enum, so nothing the compiler checks stands between a token and a reader. I
counted the direct comparison sites rather than estimating them: 16 non-test files
under plugins/frank-exchange-of-views/tools/ contain `.Type == "`, with 46
occurrences in total — capture.go 2, cli/lens/verify.go 1, record/avenue.go 3,
record/blueedit.go 2, record/citationid.go 4, record/estoppel.go 3,
record/findingid.go 1, record/findinglabel.go 2, record/motion.go 3,
record/refs.go 1, record/replay.go 7, report/assemble.go 5, scorecard/scorecard.go
4, verify/verify.go 5, view/changes.go 1, view/view.go 2. A seventeenth file,
record/record.go, composes a type token as a write-side literal (line 178,
`Type: "register"`). Test files are excluded from all of these figures.

in this repository whose diff either introduces a new token that other code
recovers by string shape, or retires such a token, where "recovers by string
shape" means a regex, a Contains, a Sprintf, a map key lookup, an equality
comparison against a literal, or a switch case — the reader classes
facts-are-fields enumerates. A change that renames a Go symbol without touching a
string-encoded token is NOT in the denominator; it has a compiler behind it and is
a different animal.

2. THE DENOMINATOR IS FIXED BEFORE THE NUMERATOR IS COUNTED. Enumerate every
change satisfying (1) in a stated commit range, record N, and only then inspect
any of them for carriers. The range is stated in advance and not truncated
afterwards. If the enumeration is too large to inspect exhaustively, sample it
with a rule fixed in advance and report the sample size — never inspect the ones

3. WHAT COUNTS AS A CARRIER LEFT BEHIND. At the merge commit of the change, a site
still speaking the old model that is (i) in a tree that ships, (ii) reachable by
the vocabulary in question, and (iii) NOT annotated, in code or in the change's own

model IS the permanent dual-read under discussion, so counting it as evidence
against dual-read would make the census answer its own question. Deliberate
retention goes in a THIRD column, reported alongside, because its count is
independently interesting — it measures how often this codebase chooses dual-read
when it has the choice.

4. THE HAZARD I HAVE TO NAME BECAUSE IT CUTS AGAINST ME. Criterion (iii) is
read from the author's own text, and an author who forgot a carrier and an author
who kept it on purpose can produce the same annotation after the fact. Where the
evidence is ambiguous, the case is scored as DELIBERATE — the reading that costs me
the numerator — and the ambiguous count is reported separately so a reader can see
how much of the result rides on that call.

5. REPORTING FORM. "k of N changes left at least one carrier behind," with k, N,
the commit range, and the deliberate-retention and ambiguous counts. A bare count
of carriers with no base rate is an anecdote and does not appear. My own stated
bar — the number need not be precise to be decisive if it is materially above zero
— stands only against an N fixed in advance, which is exactly what red said, and
without it the criteria could be loosened until k is non-zero with nobody,
including me, able to tell afterwards that it happened.

6. THE DEFEATER, restated so it is reportable rather than quietly re-scoped. If
carriers were essentially always converted, then institutional memory holds,
dual-read's cost really is flat, and the report's thesis should move TOWARD
dual-read and away from mine. I will write that in those words if the census
returns it.

payload.text:
Three items from this sitting, all hit while doing the work rather than recalled.

1. `--reason-file` IS ADVERTISED ON `blue avenue` AND DOES NOT WORK ON THE MOVE
BRANCH. `blue avenue --help` lists `--reason-file` with the gloss "for anything
long or that would fight shell quoting." I called
`blue avenue --id A1 --status pursued --reason-file <path>` and got
"moving A1 requires --reason". I then tried the documented stdin form,
`--reason-file - < file`, and got the identical error. So the move branch's
required-field validation consults --reason only and never the file it was told
to read from. The workaround I used was shell command substitution —
`R="$(cat file)"; ... --reason "$R"` — which is exactly the shell quoting the flag
exists to avoid, and my A1 reason contained backticks and a Go struct tag that I
had to rewrite out of the prose to be sure the shell would not touch them. That is
a capability gap that silently degrades the content: the natural response to the
error is to shorten the reason until it fits on a command line, and a shortened
avenue reason is the whole substance of the act. Every other verb I used
(`friction`, `position`) advertises the same flag and I did not test them; the
defect may be common to the branch that validates required prose fields before
resolving them, and the fix should sweep the siblings rather than patch avenue.

2. THE BENCH GRANTED ME RELIEF THAT NO SITTING EXISTS TO DISCHARGE. The petition
ruling holds that "Blue's obligation in the coming round is to draft the report."
This sitting's dispatch scopes me to one job — answering red's rulings on my lines
— and inputs/run-config.json sets maxRounds to 2, so this IS the coming round and
there is no later blue sitting. The run therefore closes with blue/report.md at
176 bytes: three acceptance checks the bench expressly said are scoreable against
"whatever blue produces," and blue produces nothing. I am not asking to be
relieved of anything; I am reporting that a granted relief and the round budget
contradict each other, and the contradiction is invisible from inside either one.
What the work wanted: the engine to reconcile granted relief against the remaining
round budget before dispatching, and to say so loudly if the round that owes the
relief does not exist. This is the second time in one run that a bench direction
has had no carrier — the bench itself reported that its direction to red could not
be delivered — and both failures have the same shape: the ruling is written, and
nothing downstream is obliged to notice it.

3. NO TERMINAL FATE FOR A LINE THAT RAN AND ANSWERED. The avenue status enum is
proposed | pursued | declined | abandoned | deferred. A1 and A5 were run to a
result in this sitting: A1's hypothesis was FALSIFIED — the census I built to
defeat my own R1-1 pricing failed to defeat it — and A5 produced its bound with a
named unmeasured residue. Neither is "pursued" in the sense the gloss gives
("being followed"), which reads as in-flight; neither is "abandoned," which the
gloss defines as pursued-then-died and which would falsely say the line yielded
nothing. So I recorded both as `pursued` and put the outcome in prose, which means
the single most decisive fact this sitting produced — that a disconfirming line was
run and came back negative — is recoverable only by reading a long reason field,
not from any field a projection could count. That is this repository's own
facts-are-fields failure inside the tool that enforces it: the fate of a hypothesis
is a fact another party acts on, and it is currently prose. What the work wanted:
a terminal status (`answered`, or `pursued` plus a required
`--hypothesis-outcome confirmed|falsified|inconclusive`) so that "blue ran a
disconfirming line and lost it" is a field, and so a later reader can count how
many hypotheses this system actually tested rather than how many it proposed.

This sitting had one job — answer red's rulings on A1 through A6 — and I decided
each on its reason rather than on its verdict. Two lines I ran rather than
re-filed. Three I deferred with the reason stated as a fact about this run's
budget. One I declined, accepting red's method argument and contesting the
substitute red offered in its place. As in round 1 I made no edit to
blue/report.md, so there is no `revision` event and no CHANGELOG entry: a receipt
with no artifact behind it is worse than a gap in the record.

WHAT I RAN, AND WHAT IT COST ME.

A1 — PURSUED, HYPOTHESIS FALSIFIED. I proposed this census specifically because it
could kill my own R1-1 pricing, and red endorsed it for that reason. It did not
kill it, and the reason it did not is a measurement rather than an argument. At
pin 0783a2c the event vocabulary has no chokepoint: the type token is recovered by
string comparison at 46 sites across 16 non-test files under
plugins/frank-exchange-of-views/tools/ (counted per file, not estimated —
replay.go 7, assemble.go 5, verify.go 5, citationid.go 4, scorecard.go 4, and
eleven others), Event.Type is a plain Go string rather than a typed enum, and the
shard-open path is implemented TWICE: record/replay.go line 103 is canonical, and
capture/capture.go line 460 opens the same files independently and decodes each
line into map[string]any, recovering the type as a bare map key lookup that never
touches the record package. Red's regrade on R1-1 was expressly provisional — "a
census finding one exported entry point restores low." There is no such point. The
provisional does not fire and medium-high stands, on evidence I built to break it.

I also accepted red's precondition and then verified it more widely than red did.
Red's grep was restricted to '*.go' and to five token names, which could not have
found a non-Go reader had one existed. I re-ran it across the whole tree in every
language, without truncation: no source file outside plugins/ references records/
or events-*.jsonl at the pin at all — the only non-plugins hits are markdown,
JSON data, and other runs' artifacts, and the single non-Go file that mentions a
run's .jsonl is debate.js line 199, naming the trajectory files agent-*.jsonl in
prompt prose rather than opening them. So red's collapse of my two cells is right
on a wider probe than red's own, and the population is settled as red's reading
(a): the readers are the AUTHOR'S OWN CODE, shipped into installations the author
cannot observe. What varies across that population is version currency, not
authorship, and that axis is unobservable from the tree by construction.

A5 — PURSUED, AND IT CORRECTED ME IN MY FAVOUR AND THEN AGAINST ME. The delivery
hops in the pinned corpus are static and outbound: marketplace.json carries a
name, an owner, and four plugin entries with relative source paths; each
plugin.json carries name, version, description, author, license, dependencies,
keywords. No field at either hop can be populated by a consumer and no code in the
tree receives one. The trace stops at /plugin update, which is client behaviour
outside the pin, and I stopped it there explicitly rather than guessing across the
boundary.

The correction in my favour: I had proposed to say the published vocabulary set is
"observable with certainty," and I went to check whether that certainty was a rule
or a mechanism, because this run's own R1-1 is about the difference.
scripts/versionguard/main.go fails a pull request whose plugin content changed
without the version moving, comparing against the merge-base rather than the
branch tip, and .github/workflows/hooks.yml line 213 runs it in CI. So the strong
half of the bound is backed rather than assumed. Its header also states, in the
author's own words and without reference to this debate, that it is "Dev tooling
for this repository only. Nothing here ships to an installing project" — an
independent confirmation of the structural claim my R1-1 dispute rested on.

The correction against me is the one I care more about. My proposed second
sentence was that the installed set is "not observable at all." What I actually
established is that the DELIVERY ARTIFACTS carry nothing back. The distribution
host is a different thing: a git host's clone and fetch logs are a real signal an
author can sometimes read, and that host is outside the pin and outside anything I
inspected. So the honest second sentence is bounded twice — unobservable from the
delivery artifacts, with the host-side residue UNMEASURED rather than zero. On a
topic whose entire subject is a miss that looks like a zero, I am not going to
write the run's own error into the run's own report.

And A5 does NOT reach R1-3, which I say plainly because the temptation runs the
other way. Red rejected that dispute on my report's ARCHITECTURE — that my own
position statement puts unobservability in the keystone — not on the fact. A line
that confirms a premise red never contested overturns nothing, and re-disputing on
it would be closure-shopping. The grade stands and belongs on the drafted text.

WHAT I DECLINED, AND THE PIECE OF THE RULING I DID NOT TAKE.

A4 — DECLINED AS PROPOSED. Red's censoring argument defeats the line and I accept
it without hedging: a failure never detected produces no document and cannot enter
the sample at any latency, so my proposed remedy — measure WHEN rather than
WHETHER — does not uncensor anything. I named that bias in the proposal and did
not fix it; red noticed I had not fixed it. Red offered a route back — name three
reachable primary documents before spending the budget — and I am not taking it,
because I would be naming sources I have not opened, which is the exact failure
the bench corrected me on in this same run while granting my petition. Losing a
line is cheaper than repeating that.

What I do not accept is that the redirect asks "the identical question." A2's
harness run the other way measures whether a signal is EMITTED. A4 asked whether
it is DETECTED. My own concession is that migration fails loudly "at a known
point, in front of someone who is watching" — and a harness cannot establish that
anyone was watching, in a population defined by the author's inability to look. An
emitted error nobody reads is a plausible zero with extra steps. Red drew this
exact distinction twice in these rulings, against my A5 and in A2's floor
condition, and called it the recurring hazard of the topic; I am applying it to
red's own substitute. So I am carrying a requirement stricter than the one red
imposed: even with both harness arms run, the report must not state the asymmetry
as measured, because both arms measure emission, and the case record for this
migration shape was not searched. If a later sitting lets that sentence drift back
into "migration fails visibly," the regression is mine to answer.

WHAT I DEFERRED, AND WHY THAT IS THE HONEST WORD.

A2, A3 and A6 are deferred, and the reason is the same in each case and is not a
judgement about the lines. `blue prove` and `blue cite` both anchor to an exact
sentence in blue/report.md. blue/report.md is 176 bytes with no prose. maxRounds
is 2 and this is the round-2 blue sitting. A number or a citation produced now has
nowhere on the record to land, and recording those lines as pursued would be a
receipt for work the artifact does not contain. A3 is the one that stings: red
endorsed it without conditions and said to run it first if budget forced a choice.
The budget forced the choice and I could not run it, so the proposition R1-2's
high impact rests on — that dual-read's miss mode is a silent plausible zero —
ends this run exactly as it began: argued, instantiated locally, and never tested
against the systems that made the strictness choice on purpose.

I did discharge red's A6 condition rather than defer it with the line. The
inclusion criteria for the carrier-decay census are now fixed on a timestamped
record BEFORE any walk: what counts as a conceptual change naming a vocabulary,
that the denominator N is enumerated before any case is inspected, and that a
carrier deliberately retained is scored in a separate column because it IS the
dual-read under discussion rather than evidence against it. Ambiguous cases score
as deliberate — the reading that costs me the numerator — and the ambiguous count
is reported separately. I put this in the record rather than in a file beside the
report on purpose: a criteria document nothing can refuse is the shape this
repository names as a defect, and the event log is timestamped where a markdown
file is not.

The decay anchor is now n=2 rather than n=1, and I found the second one without
looking for it. versionguard exists because on 2026-07-31 pull requests #198 and
#195 merged hours apart, #195 branched earlier and merging on top, so main kept
both features' content and reverted prosthetic-conscience's version to 0.21.0 —
one already shipped. In the file's own words: "Every consumer who had pulled
0.21.0 would therefore never receive the strike counter, and nothing anywhere
would have said so. No test failed. No guard fired." That is the plausible zero
crossing the publish boundary in this tree, with a date and two pull request
numbers. Two instances is not a rate and I am not reporting it as one.

WHERE I STAND, unchanged in direction and better anchored in one place and worse
in another. My position is still that the permanent dual-read is the more
expensive option for this shape of log, and I still hold it at medium confidence.
A1 strengthened the mechanical half — 46 string-shaped recovery sites and a second
independent parser are a wide surface for a retired token to fail quietly across,
and capture.go's silent skip is one reader already sitting in the cell A2 was
convened to count. Nothing this sitting touched the half that matters most,
because A3 did not run. I would rather end the run saying that than end it with
six lines marked proposed and a thesis that never met a test.
